source_text: καίων εἰς σωτηρίαν· ὁποῖοί τινες γεγόνασιν Ὑμέναιός τε καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος, οἰόμενοί τε καὶ λέγοντες ἀνάστασιν ἤδη γεγονέναι. Καὶ προστεθεῖεν ἂν τούτοις, οἱ ἀπονεύοντες ἀχαλίνως πρὸς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν τῶν ἐκτόπων, καὶ τῆς ἑαυτῶν διανοίας τὸν καρπὸν παραῤῥιπτοῦντες ἁπλῶς εἰς ἑώλους καὶ ἀσελγεῖς ἡδονάς. Οὐκοῦν ὁ λεπρὸς μὲν καὶ γονοῤῥυὴς, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ὁ τοῖς νεκρότητος ἔργοις ἐνισχημένος (εἶεν δ' ἂν ἔργα νεκρότητος, τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς πάθη), καὶ ὁ τὴν ἔσω καρποφορίαν, τὴν εἰς νοῦν δηλονότι καὶ κεκρυμμένην, οὐκ ἀπαρ
pass_a_gloss: §9 dual gloss: ἁπτόμενος / touch; ἑρπετοῦ / creeping thing … Pass A literal scaffolding ≠ Pass B continuous English. Theme: Hymenaeus/Alexander; unworthy eating; touching uncleanness =
pass_b_english: Cyril: …sary unto salvation; of which sort Hymenaeus and Alexander have become, both thinking and saying resurrection has already happened. And to these would be added those inclining unbridledly toward anything whatsoever of the outlandish, and simply casting aside the fruit of their own mind unto stale and wanton pleasures. So then the leprous and the one with flow of seed, that is, the one held in works of deadness (and works of deadness would be the passions of the flesh), and the one not having the inward fruit-bearing, clearly the unto mind and hidden, uncorrupted, let him withdraw, he says, from the holy things, until he should be cleansed. For as all-divine Paul said, ‘Whoever should eat the body of the Lord and drink his cup unworthily, eats and drinks judgment for himself, not discerning his body. But let a human,’ he says, ‘test himself, and then eat from the bread, and drink from the cup.’

Cyril: So then observe, O Palladius, the accuracy of the law; for it has least gone against only the leprous and the one with flow of seed, but as it were also condemns-with them, even if somehow someone should touch those sick, I mean leprous and with flow of seed. ‘And the one touching,’ he says, ‘every uncleanness of soul, or for whom a bed of his seed should go out, will be unclean.’
Palladius: And what damage from this would become for those touching?

Cyril: None at least, according to the word in ready hand. For touch of body will not defile a human’s soul. But the law is spiritual, and teaches us again riddlingly, that unclean in charges of pollutions are those liable to soul-passions. And those touching are defiled-with them, or clinging, clearly according to relation of same-counsel, or same-deed; ‘For evil companies corrupt good customs’; and, ‘No share for a faithful with an unfaithful’; and enemy and irreconcilable to the dark is the light. And true that ‘With a holy one you will be holy, and with an innocent man you will be innocent, and with a chosen one you will be chosen, and with a crooked one you will twist.’ And that not only being sick the most outlandish of the passions will be all-hard for those sick alone, but also whoever should become same-minded and same-opinioned will be defiled with pollutions not less than those, he showed at once adding, that ‘Whoever if he should touch every unclean creeping thing will defile him, or upon a human in whom he defiles according to every uncleanness of him, a soul which should touch them will be unclean until evening.’ And bitter and venom-shooting creeping things we say both to be said and to be those for whom the word would be fitting, ‘Venom of asps under their lips; whose mouth is full of curse and bitterness.’ And these would be also before the others those twisting the straight things, and sounding into the simpler ones the word that procures destruction, carrying them off toward thoughts not good, and unto glory upon God the
